item.title: Resynthesising the Traditional: Fragmented Distance (CTM x NOPA Artistic Lab, Armenia)
item.description:
Organisation: CTM Festival with NOPA Festival

Location: Yerevan / Armenia. Preference to artists who reside in or have a diasporic connection to Armenia, Georgia, Iran, Iraq, Syria, the Anatolian region, the Caspian Sea, the Levant, and the Northern Caucasus.

Award: Participants supported with a travel budget of up to EUR 450 each, accommodation and catering for the duration of the lab, a NOPA Festival pass, and a per diem. Visa fees supported when required, and letters of invitation provided. Free to apply.

Duration: Eight-day lab, 1 to 10 October 2026 (arrival 1 October, departure 10 October)

Deadline: Closed 08 Aug 2026

Fragmented Distance is the latest artistic lab from CTM Festival's Resynthesising the Traditional initiative (co-curated by Stas Sharifulla and CTM), taking place 1 to 10 October 2026 in Armenia in collaboration with NOPA, a festival dedicated to sonic arts and experimental music. Resynthesising the Traditional explores how musicians, sound artists, and researchers can critically engage with traditions and heritage, using resynthesis (a computer-music method that analyses sounds to extract their fundamental components) as a guiding metaphor, and resisting conservative views of culture as frozen or untouchable; the lab is an open toolbox helping artists connect to 'the traditional' outside of exoticisation, cultural essentialism, and uneven power dynamics. This edition focuses on diaspora, memory, displacement, transmission, and hybridity, responding to Armenia's shift into a point of arrival for refugees and diasporic communities and to the displacement following the ethnic cleansing of Artsakh / Nagorno-Karabakh. It invites artists whose work resynthesising traditional practices addresses how traditional musical forms are maintained, altered, or recontextualised as they move across geographies and generations, how in-betweenness and non-belonging can be articulated through sound, and how sonic expression can act as rehumanisation. THE LAB (eight days, 10:00-19:00 daily) includes theory and practice workshops, individual closed oral presentations, solo public performances (15-20 minutes), specialist inputs, guided sonic improvisations, field trips, and feedback sessions. Following the lab, participants may propose new solo or collaborative work to the Resynthesising the Traditional team; selected works are shortlisted for commission and presentation at CTM Festival Berlin and/or NOPA Festival Yerevan. CONDITIONS: solo artists/projects only; applicants should have an existing practice tied to (re)connecting with traditional ideas and sounds through a contemporary lens, and clear next steps; working knowledge of English recommended. SELECTION: a pre-selection committee (Varoujan Chetirian, Stas Sharifulla, Taica Replansky) creates a shortlist, from which up to six participants are chosen by lab co-hosts Cinna Peyghamy, Vardan Baghdasaryan, and Varoujan Chetirian. TIMELINE: deadline 8 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST; results by early September 2026; lab 1 to 10 October 2026. Apply with a portfolio (PDF, max 10 pages) and an audio link; questions to team@nopa.art. Free to apply.

item.title: Mondriaan Fund: Inside-Out Art Museum Residency 2027 (Beijing)
item.description:
Organisation: Mondriaan Fund / Inside-Out Art Museum

Location: Beijing, China. For visual artists, curators and critics based in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom, funded by the Mondriaan Fund.

Award: Subsidy of EUR 8,478 for an artist or EUR 5,622 for a curator/critic toward travel, material and living costs (a 10 percent personal contribution is automatically deducted by the Mondriaan Fund); studio, living space and Inside-Out Art Museum support are paid directly by the Mondriaan Fund. For a selected duo the total is increased proportionally to cover the second applicant's travel and accommodation. Contribution for Caribbean-based residents can be increased for higher travel costs. No application fee.

Duration: Three months: 1 March to 30 May 2027 (flexible start date, set by IOAM in consultation with the resident)

Deadline: 27 Aug 2026

Mondriaan Fund-supported working period at Inside-Out Art Museum (IOAM) in Beijing, one of China's leading independent platforms for contemporary art and research. The museum combines exhibitions, critical inquiry and public programmes, giving residents room for in-depth research, experimentation and exchange within a Chinese art scene that is otherwise hard to access from Europe. The residency is framed as cultural exchange rather than production to deadline: IOAM works with a flexible model that takes the resident's other obligations into account and sets the exact start date in consultation with the selected candidate. WHO: visual artists, curators and critics based in the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. Duos and collaborations may apply (two artists, two curators/critics, or a combination who structurally make work together, submitting a joint plan for the work period that leads to a single result, and who live and work together in the same space during the residency), but each individual must submit a separate application; the apartment is well suited to duos or partnerships. WORK PERIOD: one period of three months, 1 March to 30 May 2027, with room for one artist or duo; you can state a preference for the work period in the application form. Selection is by advisory committee; read the Mondriaan Fund Residency explanation for the conditions, assessment and checklist, plus the fund's general terms and conditions, before applying. DEADLINE: Thursday 27 August 2026, before 16:00 Dutch time / 10:00 Caribbean time.

item.title: Project Tech4Dev: AI Cohort Program 3.0 (NGOs building AI solutions)
item.description:
Organisation: Project Tech4Dev

Location: Remote cohort programme. No geographic restriction is stated in the call, but the framing is India-centred: preference goes to problems involving multi-modal input and Indic languages.

Award: FLAG, UNVERIFIED: no grant amount, stipend, fee or compute credit is stated. What the call describes is hands-on implementation support, mentorship and expert guidance across three sprints; participating NGOs must invest one person's full bandwidth for the duration.

Duration: Six months, tentatively mid-September 2026 to January or February 2027 (subject to change)

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

The third round of Project Tech4Dev's AI Cohort, a hands-on implementation programme for NGOs designing, building and deploying responsible AI solutions inside their own programmes. Cohort 2.0 worked with seven NGOs across education, civic engagement, youth development and nonprofit technology, who built and piloted AI teaching assistants, volunteer coaches, mentoring tools and decision-support systems; the organisers' stated lesson was that adoption turns on understanding user needs, testing rapidly, measuring impact and building responsibly rather than on the technology itself. Cohort 3.0 is aimed at organisations ready to move past exploration into solutions that can be deployed in real-world settings. STRUCTURE (three sprints over roughly six months): Discovery Sprint (months 1 to 2) covering problem discovery, use-case prioritisation, data-readiness assessment, user research and solution design; Build Sprint (months 2 to 5) covering prototype development, implementation sprints, user testing, mentorship and responsible AI evaluations; and Activation Sprint (month 6) covering pilot deployment, impact assessment, operationalisation planning and a final showcase with peers and ecosystem partners. SELECTION CRITERIA: NGOs must show some in-house technical or data capability, ideally a dedicated person who can anchor the work (not necessarily an AI expert, but able to manage workflows, communicate operational requirements and work with mentors and experts); must commit one person's full bandwidth for the whole programme, including aligning leadership, adapting operations and making room to test, monitor and refine; and preference goes to problems involving multi-modal input, especially Indic languages, and to use cases built on LLMs. Applications are open to nonprofits across sectors, with priority to climate-focused organisations whose AI use cases could improve programme delivery, decision-making or community outcomes. Apply via the Google Form linked from the announcement before 10 August 2026.

item.title: G.MAP Digital Art Culture Lab 2026: Project Lab (Gwangju, South Korea)
item.description:
Organisation: Gwangju Media Art Platform (G.MAP)

Location: Jeonnam-Gwangju, South Korea. International applicants welcome (Track 2 only).

Award: Track 2 (Interdisciplinary Creation): creation and production grant up to KRW 30,000,000 per team, plus accommodation, equipment, studio space, production and travel support, exhibition on G.MAP spaces and large-scale public media platforms (LED Wall, city media facades), and publication. Free to apply.

Duration: Five-month creation support program, August to December 2026

Deadline: Closed 09 Aug 2026

The Gwangju Media Art Platform (G.MAP), an institution of Gwangju, UNESCO Creative City of Media Arts, invites artists and teams working in digital art to the 2026 Digital Art Culture Lab: Project Lab, a five-month creation support program (August to December 2026) covering the entire creative process from idea development through production, showcase and archiving. WHO CAN APPLY: artists and groups in digital art wishing to create interdisciplinary projects using digital technology (all members aged 19+; international applicants welcome). Focus areas: digital art, media art, generative art, AI, interactive art, XR, AR, VR, interdisciplinary, art and technology. SELECTION: 14 teams total across two tracks: Track 1 Digital Transformation (7 artists/teams) and Track 2 Interdisciplinary Creation (7 teams). INTERNATIONAL ARTISTS CAN APPLY FOR TRACK 2 ONLY. SUPPORT: creation and production grant up to KRW 30,000,000 per team for Track 2, two online mentoring sessions, and a showcase in G.MAP exhibition spaces and on large-scale public media platforms including the G.MAP LED Wall and city media facades. KEY DATES: application period 21 July to 9 August 2026, 6 PM KST; results announced 14 August 2026; program period 20 August to 31 December 2026. Overseas participants (Track 2) must attend two in-person meetings in Jeonnam-Gwangju. HOW TO APPLY: submit the application form and portfolio (PDF) by email to uartlabseoul@gmail.com. More info at urbanartlab.org/opencall. Free to apply.

Open call details

item.title: Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation: Inlaks Theatre Art Award 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation

Location: India. Open to Indian citizens.

Award: INR 15,000 per month for up to 12 months, around INR 180,000 total (roughly USD 2,050 / EUR 1,780). No application fee.

Duration: Up to twelve months of skill enhancement, with six-month interim and final reporting.

Deadline: Closed 15 Aug 2026

A skill-enhancement award for emerging Indian theatre practitioners, supporting participation in recognised training workshops, residencies and similar programmes rather than the production of a specific work. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: Indian citizens born after 1 January 1991, with preference given to holders of a theatre degree from a leading Indian institution. Recipients report at the six-month mark and on completion. Applications close 15 August 2026 at 23:59 IST via Submittable. The foundation runs several other awards on adjacent deadlines, including the Inlaks-Attakkalari Dance Studentship (30 August 2026) and a two-month Inlaks Residency at the International Center of Photography in the USA for emerging Indian photographic practitioners (31 August 2026).

item.title: India Foundation for the Arts: Arts Research Programme (May 2026 Request for Proposals)
item.description:
Organisation: India Foundation for the Arts (IFA)

Location: India; project-based with no residency requirement. Open to Indian nationals only.

Award: Up to INR 500,000 (around USD 5,700 / EUR 4,900) per project. Honorarium is capped at 35 percent of the budget. Institutional overhead, building costs, infrastructure and equipment purchases are excluded. No application fee.

Duration: Minimum 12 months, maximum 18 months.

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

IFA's Arts Research Programme funds research into forms of knowing and thinking rooted in creative, scholarly or cultural practice. It explicitly welcomes experimental and self-reflexive methodologies, practice-based inquiry, interdisciplinary dialogue, community engagement, translation studies and work on marginalised narratives, with a shareable public outcome expected. Open to artists, scholars, curators, translators, educators and practitioner-researchers. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: Indian nationals only, and PIO and OCI card holders are explicitly excluded; any collaborators must also be Indian nationals. Applicants need a PAN card and valid ID. PROCESS NOTE: this is a two-stage email application, not a web form. Applicants were expected to discuss the project concept with the Programme Officer (harshita@indiaifa.org) by 11 July 2026, with the final proposal, CV and budget breakdown emailed by 10 August 2026 at 23:59 IST, in an email no larger than 25 MB. Proposals may be written in any Indian language, including English.

item.title: Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation: Inlaks Fine Art Award 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation

Location: India. Open to Indian citizens currently living in India.

Award: INR 300,000 (around USD 3,400 / EUR 2,950) for one year, plus a fully covered four-week art residency at an Indian art institution. No application fee.

Duration: Twelve months of independent practice, including a mandatory four-week residency within India.

Deadline: Closed 15 Aug 2026

A one-year award enabling an emerging Indian visual artist to pursue independent practice, with a stipulation to attend a recognised art residency programme in India for four weeks during the year. ELIGIBILITY IS RESTRICTED: Indian citizens currently living in India, born on or after 1 January 1996, who are either recent graduates, postgraduates or final-year students of a leading Indian visual arts institute, or artists without those formal credentials but with a record of exhibition participation. First-year MA students are not eligible. Awardees submit progress reports at six months and on completion, plus documentation of the residency. Applications close 15 August 2026 at 23:59 IST via Submittable. Shortlisting is expected in late October 2026 with interviews in early November.
